summary: The Bradley-Terry background is densely cited, but the paper's actual subject (small adversarial or influential edits to ranking data), the accuracy of first-order group-removal approximations, and the sports comparison data are thinly supported and justify three targeted retrievals.
missing_literatures: data poisoning and adversarial manipulation of ranking / rank-aggregation / rating systems
accuracy and failure modes of first-order (group) influence approximations
Bradley-Terry / Elo rating of sports teams (NBA) as a comparison-data setting

rewrite_targets.reason: The paper's core question is how few edited or reversed comparison rows change the top rank, i.e. a data-poisoning / manipulation attack on a ranking. Related Work covers BT estimation, sampling uncertainty, influence functions and two Arena-specific manipulation papers, but cites nothing on influence-based poisoning, label-flip attacks, or adversarial manipulation of rank aggregation and rating systems. A reviewer would ask how the probe relates to that literature, and the draft cannot position its 'generic, evaluator-verified probe' without it.
rewrite_targets.anchor_text: Influence and robustness to dropping data / Integrity of crowd-sourced leaderboards paragraphs
search_topics: data poisoning attacks using influence functions
label-flipping attacks on logistic or pairwise-comparison models
adversarial manipulation and robustness of rank aggregation from pairwise comparisons

rewrite_targets.reason: Property (i) in the influence-search subsection (additive per-row effects, inaccurate at a 2% budget) and the 'Linearisation error' hypothesis in the analysis section assert limits of first-order approximations for multi-row removal without any citation. Only the single-point influence-function paper and the dropping-data robustness paper are cited. Literature on group-influence accuracy and on when infinitesimal-jackknife / influence approximations fail would ground these caveats.
rewrite_targets.anchor_text: (i) Additivity. The per-row effects are summed without modelling how p_i and A change
search_topics: accuracy of influence functions for group effects when removing multiple training points
infinitesimal jackknife approximation error for dropping data in M-estimators / logistic regression

rewrite_targets.reason: The Evaluation designs subsection and Table 1 introduce NBA game results as a fourth design and the Limitations section calls it a 'sports proxy', but no work on Bradley-Terry or Elo-style rating of sports teams is cited. One or two citations would justify using game results as BT comparison data and contextualise the home-team-first and tie conventions. The Arena and MT-Bench rows are already cited.
rewrite_targets.anchor_text: Sports & NBA regular-season games of 2008, 2012, 2015; home team listed first
search_topics: Bradley-Terry model for rating sports teams with home advantage
Elo rating system applied to basketball or team sports outcomes
